scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me not to make my 7-year-old brother go to sleep when he stayed up late watching a movie with my friend. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know my brother is sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough, he's all out of sorts the next day. That makes sense because kids his age need a lot of sleep. Last night, my mom left me in charge and trusted me to handle things. I made sure he went to bed on time, but then he woke up and came downstairs. My friend was over, and they started getting him riled up. I told him to go back to bed, but my friend said it was okay to let him stay. I was in a tough spot. If I tried to force him to go to bed, he would probably throw a fit, which would be embarrassing and exhausting. Plus, my friend was there, and I didn't want to cause a scene. So I let him stay, and by the time the movie ended, he was almost asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him in bed around midnight. The next morning, he was cranky and didn't want to get up, even though he's not allowed to sleep past 8 on weekends. My mom found out and got mad at me. I told her that since he's 7, he should know about consequences and that staying up late would make him feel bad. I also mentioned that missing two hours of sleep isn't a big deal for a kid his age. But she was still upset. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by not making him go to bed. On one hand, I didn't want to deal with the tantrum and the embarrassment. On the other hand, I know he needs his sleep, and staying up late affected him the next day. Maybe I should have been firmer and put him to bed, even if it meant some short-term discomfort. I also think about the fact that he's 7 and might not fully understand the consequences of staying up late. It's my responsibility as his older brother to make sure he gets enough sleep, even if it's hard in the moment. Maybe I should have explained why it's important to go to bed on time, even if he didn't want to. Another thing to consider is how my friend influenced the situation. My friend wanted to let him stay, which might have made it harder for me to enforce the bedtime. I should have been more assertive and set the limit, even if it meant disappointing my friend a little. In the end, while it was tough in the moment, I think it was the right decision to make sure he gets enough sleep. It's important for his health and well-being, and as his older brother, I need to prioritize that even when it's difficult.
